messages:
amanda: quick follow-up from the RFC review — we need to nail down how SLA-backed billing events (per-token) flow through the pipeline and how we store an immutable audit trail. TL;DR: current v1 events drop attribution in cache hits and we can't reconcile credits reliably.
ryan: can you summarize the concrete gap? is it about missing attribution on cached responses, or about merged partial token counts from streaming?
sandeep: both. cache hits often just emit cache_hit:true with no per-tenant token delta. streaming + function-calls split tokens across subcalls and we currently emit multiple small events with no stable id to aggregate. that breaks billing reconciliation and audits.
ellie: +1. From customer side: they see billed tokens != observable requests in logs. We need deterministic aggregation keys and an immutable write path for audit.
amanda: proposal: introduce billing_event.v2 with these core bits:
````
- event_id (uuid)
- aggregate_key (tenant_id + model_variant + request_root_id)
- token_count_total
- token_breakdown: [prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, tool_tokens]
- cache_status: {hit|miss|partial, cache_key?}
- attribution_map: [ {span_id, contributor, token_count} ]
- provenance: [ingest_node, runtime_node, timestamp_ms]
- signatures: hmac(client_key) / server_sign
````
This gives us one canonical event per user request, with ability to merge partials by event_id or aggregate_key.
ryan: sounds good. a couple tradeoffs: adding provenance + signatures increases event size and write cost. Do we plan to store full attribution_map in the main metering index or as a sidecar?
sandeep: I'd prefer sidecar storage (cold column) for heavy attribution details. Main index keeps event_id, tenant, totals, status, routing refs. sidecar (object-store + immutable manifest) for audit retrieval.
ellie: sidecar approach also helps retention policies for PII-sensitive attribution. we can redact contributor identifiers in main index.
amanda: agree. next: how to handle cache hits where we didn't compute token breakdown because response served from prefix cache? options: 1) emit an inferred event with cache_status=hit and token_count_total estimated by heuristics; 2) require runtime to compute token_delta on cache read and emit full v2; 3) lazy materialize on audit only.
ryan: (2) gives best accuracy but increases latency on hot path. (1) is cheapest but hurts audits. (3) complicates reconciliation.
sandeep: my vote: (2) but do it incrementally — runtime emits a minimal event synchronously (event_id + cache_status=hit + estimated_tokens) and a guaranteed follow-up reconciliation event within 5s if we can compute exact tokens offline. reconciliation would be idempotent and write to sidecar+index.
amanda: that fits SLOs if we cap on-path work. need to ensure we don't double-bill during reconciliation. use reconciliation flags: event_version and settled=true when final. billing engine only charges settled events or applies delta adjustments.
ellie: important: for streaming/function-calls, we need a stable request_root_id that spans subrequests and tool calls. current request_id is ephemeral per shard. propose adding request_root_id propagated in headers and runtime context.
ryan: technical note: when we propagate root id across services, we need backpressure safety — keep the id small (uuid v4) and avoid attaching massive metadata to headers.
sandeep: implementation plan:
- runtime: emit v2 minimal on first touch (event_id, aggregate_key, estimated tokens, status)
- aggregator: group by aggregate_key/event_id, apply idempotent merges, store main index row, write sidecar object on finalization
- writer: sidecar objects go to S3 with manifest and put-mutex via dynamo to ensure immutability
- billing: consume settled events from main index and apply delta adjustments as reconciliation events arrive
- audit UI: link to sidecar manifest and show before/after reconciliation diffs
amanda: owners: runtime -> ryan, aggregator/writer -> sandeep, audit UI -> ellie. I'll draft a short runbook for reconciliation race conditions and test cases.
ryan: I'll prototype header propagation and minimal sync emit. also add feature flag to gate v2.
sandeep: I'll sketch the aggregator merge logic and idempotency guarantees. thinking CRDT-lite with last-writer-wins by event_version + signed manifest to prevent replay.
ellie: test cases we need: cache-hit reconciliation, streaming split with 10 tool calls, partition failover where aggregator restarts mid-merge, and redaction flow for GDPR requests.
amanda: can infra add a short-term retention waiver for sidecar writes until we validate size? @infra-bot please create a temp quota increase for s3 writes for eng-platform team for 48h. :eyes:
infra-bot: created request #9876 for S3 write quota bump, approver: finance_eng. ETA 2h.
ryan: noted, I'll add telemetry to measure extra bytes/event and CPU cost for signing.
sandeep: one more: we should include a small change to existing token attribution export for audits (CSV) to include event_version and event_id so downstream finance can reconcile.
ellie: ok, actionable items captured. Amanda, if you can post the short RFC amendment with these points I'll convert to a follow-up RFC and schedule a 30m sync next week. :thumbsup:
amanda: will do. thanks all.
